# Processes

## Overview

Processes define the production workflows your organisation uses to fulfil jobs — for example, "Digital Printing", "Framing", "Film Development", or "Photo Restoration". Each process can have its own colour, default settings, and location routing rules.

When an order arrives, each job is assigned a process based on its product category. This determines how the job appears on the Production Board, which location handles it, and what print settings are applied.

Manage processes from **Settings → Processes**.

---

## Creating a Process

1. Navigate to **Settings → Processes**.
2. Click **Add Process**.
3. Fill in the details:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Process Name** | A descriptive name (e.g. "Digital Printing", "Canvas Stretch", "Framing"). |
| **Description** | Optional notes about what this process covers. |
| **Badge Color** | The colour used to identify this process on the Production Board and job cards. Choose from Blue, Green, Purple, Orange, Red, Yellow, Pink, or Cyan. |
| **Default Print Size** | The default print size applied to jobs in this process (e.g. "4x6", "8x10"). Can be overridden per job. |
| **Default Copies** | The default number of copies for jobs in this process. Defaults to 1. |

4. Click **Save**.

---

## Linking Categories to Processes

Product categories are automatically registered when orders are received from your connected websites. Once a category exists, you can assign it to a process.

1. Navigate to **Settings → Categories** (or the category management section).
2. Click **View Details** on a category.
3. In the category detail modal, select the **Process** from the dropdown.
4. Optionally configure **Lead Time** (in business days) and **Production Days** (which days of the week this category is produced).
5. Save the changes.

### What this controls

- **Production Board grouping** — Jobs are filtered and displayed by their assigned process.
- **Due date calculation** — The lead time and production days determine when a job is due, based on the order date.
- **Default settings** — The process's default print size and copies are applied to new jobs in that category.

### Unassigned categories

Categories that have not been linked to a process appear in the **Unassigned Categories** alert on the Dashboard. This helps you catch new product types that need configuration.

### Standalone processes

Some jobs (e.g. "Photo Restoration" or custom services) may not come from a website category. These are matched to a process by name — if a process exists with the same name as the service, it is automatically linked. These items appear under the **Services** section and allow free-text product input.

---

## Ordering Processes

Processes are displayed in a defined order on the Production Board and in dropdowns. Use the **up and down arrows** next to each process to reorder them.

The display order affects:
- The sequence of process filter options.
- The order in which processes appear in selection dropdowns.

---

## Disable Sending to OrderHub Downloader

Each process has a toggle: **Disable Sending to OrderHub Downloader**.

When enabled, jobs assigned to this process will **not** appear in the OHD pending download queue. Use this for processes that do not require artwork to be downloaded to a local workstation — for example, a "Pickup Only" or "External Fulfilment" process.

---

## Location Overrides

By default, a job's production location is determined by the order's **pickup location** — the store where the customer will collect their order. Location overrides let you route jobs with a specific process to different locations instead.

### When to use

- A central production facility handles all printing, regardless of which store took the order.
- Framing is only done at one location, but orders can be placed at any store.
- Different processes are handled by different sites.

### Configuring an override

1. Edit the process (click the pencil icon).
2. Enable **Override Production Location**.
3. Select one or more locations from the list. Only active store locations are shown.
4. Save the process.

### How it works

- When a job is created with this process, the system checks for location overrides.
- If overrides are configured, the job is routed to the specified location(s) instead of the order's pickup location.
- The OHD API returns the override locations in the job data so that the downloader fetches artwork to the correct site.
- If no overrides are set (or the toggle is off), the job uses the order's pickup location as normal.

---

## Editing and Deleting Processes

- **Edit** — Click the pencil icon on any process to update its name, colour, defaults, OHD setting, or location overrides.
- **Delete** — Click the trash icon to remove a process. Categories previously assigned to it will become unlinked and appear in the Unassigned Categories alert.

> **Caution**: Deleting a process does not delete the jobs already assigned to it, but those jobs will no longer have a process association.

---

## Example Setup

| Process | Color | Default Size | Copies | OHD | Location Override |
|---------|-------|-------------|--------|-----|-------------------|
| Digital Printing | Blue | 4x6 | 1 | Enabled | None (uses pickup location) |
| Canvas Stretch | Purple | 16x20 | 1 | Enabled | Production Lab only |
| Framing | Orange | — | 1 | Disabled | Framing Workshop only |
| Film Development | Green | — | 1 | Enabled | None (uses pickup location) |
| Photo Restoration | Cyan | — | 1 | Disabled | None (uses pickup location) |

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Jobs not appearing on the Production Board | Check that the job's category is assigned to a process. Unassigned categories are listed in the Dashboard alert. |
| New category not showing in settings | Categories are registered when orders arrive. If the category is new, it will appear after the first order containing it is received. |
| Wrong location receiving jobs | Check whether the process has a location override enabled. Edit the process and review the selected locations. |
| Jobs appearing in OHD queue unexpectedly | Verify the **Disable Sending to OrderHub Downloader** toggle is set correctly on the process. |
| Due dates seem wrong | Check the **Lead Time** and **Production Days** configured on the category, not the process. These are set per category in the category detail modal. |
